<!-- result-1: body_md -->
\label{prop_c}
Let $\mathcal{P}^c_{\boldsymbol{\theta},\bar{F}}$ in
\eqref{eq:c_CG_sempar_model} be the constrained CG semiparametric model.
Then, the (infinite-dimensional) nuisance tangent space
$\mathcal{T}^c_{\bar{F}}$ at $\bar{F} \in \overline{\mathcal{F}}$ is given by
  
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:Tc_G0_1}
\begin{split}
\mathcal{T}^c_{\bar{F}}
&= \left\lbrace h : \mathbb{R}^{mn} \rightarrow \mathbb{R} |
h\ \text{is $\sigma(\mathcal{Q}_{mn})$-measurable},\right. \\
& \qquad \left. {\rm E}(h(\mathcal{Q}_{mn})) =0,\;
{\rm E}(\mathcal{Q}_{mn}h(\mathcal{Q}_{mn}) )=0
\right\rbrace,
\end{split}
\end{equation}
 
where $\sigma(\mathcal{Q}_{mn})\subset \mathfrak{B}(\mathcal{X})$ is the
sub-$\sigma$-algebra generated by the r.v.\
$\mathcal{Q}_{mn} =Q_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}({\bf y}_n)$ in \eqref{eq:Q_alpha},
with $\boldsymbol{\theta}$ here denoting the true parameter vector.
Moreover, the orthogonal projection of ${\bf s}_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}$ onto
$\mathcal{T}^c_{\bar{F}}$ is given by
 
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:proj_cg}
\Pi({\bf s}_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}|\mathcal{T}^c_{\bar{F}})
= {\rm E}({\bf s}_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}|\mathcal{Q}_{mn})
- {\rm E}(\mathcal{Q}_{mn}{\bf s}_{\boldsymbol{\theta}})\,
\sigma_{\mathcal{Q}_{mn}}^{-2}\,(\mathcal{Q}_{mn}-mn).
\end{equation}
<!-- end result-1 -->
<!-- result-2: body_md -->
\label{Semiparametric FIM CG}
The semiparametric efficient FIM
$\bar{\bf I}_{{\bf y}_n}(\boldsymbol{\theta}|\bar{F})$ for CG distributions
under the constraint ${\rm E}(\tau)=1$ is identical to the semiparametric
efficient FIM $\bar{\bf I}_{{\bf y}_n}(\boldsymbol{\theta}|\bar{g}_{mn})$
for ES distributions under the constraint ${\rm E}(\mathcal{Q}_{mn})=mn$, given
in \cite[eq.~(116)]{Fortunati2026} and, here, by
\eqref{eq:Slepian-Bangs's formula} with \eqref{eq:a0a1} and
\eqref{eq:a2clsepa}.
<!-- end result-2 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{property phi}
The r.v. $\varphi(\mathcal{Q}_{mn})$, which appears in the definition \eqref{eq:def xi1r} and \eqref{eq:def x2r}
of $\xi_{1,mn}$ and $\xi_{2,mn}$, respectively, can be expressed through the following conditional expectation:
 
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:phi q}
\varphi(\mathcal{Q}_{mn})
=
{\rm E}[\tau^{-1}|\mathcal{Q}_{mn}].
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{property xi 2}
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:xi 2}
\xi_{2,mn}
=
1- \frac{{\rm E}[{\rm Var}(\chi_{mn}^2|\mathcal{Q}_{mn})]}{mn(mn+2)},
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- result-3: body_md -->
\label{property FIM inequality}
For arbitrary CG distribution, 
 
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:inequality a2 clas sepa}
a_{2,mn}^{\rm SePa}
\le
a_{2,mn}^{\rm Clas},
\end{equation}
 
with equality i.f.f. the distribution is Gaussian.
<!-- end result-3 -->
<!-- result-4: body_md -->
\label{Result matrice mean limit}
 
Under the assumptions given in Section \ref{sec:Preliminaries on multidimensional stationary SIRP}, we have the limit:
 
\begin{equation}
\label{eq: matrice mean limit}
\lim_{n \rightarrow \infty}\frac{1}{n}{\boldsymbol \mu'}^T_{{\bf y}_n,k}\ \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{{\bf y}_n}^{-1}{\boldsymbol \mu}'_{{{\bf y}_n},\ell}
={\boldsymbol \mu'}^T_{{\bf x}_k}{\bf S}_{x}^{-1}(0){\boldsymbol \mu}'_{{\bf x}_\ell}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end result-4 -->
<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
For $d_n^1, d_n^2$ strictly increasing, $d_n^1 \times d_n^2$ matrices ${\bf A}_n$ and ${\bf B}_n$,
${\bf A}_n \sim {\bf B}_n$ means that:
$\|{\bf A}_n\|_2, \|{\bf B}_n\|_2 \le M <\infty$ and $\lim_{n\rightarrow \infty}\frac{\|{\bf A}_n-{\bf B}_n\|_{\rm Fro}}{\sqrt{n}}=0$ \cite[Definition 3.1]{Gutierrez2011}.
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- result-5: body_md -->
\label{Result matrice variance limit}
 
Under the assumptions given in Section \ref{sec:Preliminaries on multidimensional stationary SIRP}, we have the limits:
 
\begin{equation}
\label{eq: matrice variance limit 1}
\lim_{n \rightarrow \infty}\frac{1}{n}
{\rm Tr}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{{\bf y}_n}^{-1}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{{\bf y}_n,k}^{'})
=
\int_{0}^{1}
{\rm Tr}({\bf S}_{x}^{-1}(f) {\bf S}_{x,k}^{'}(f))df,
\end{equation}
 
\begin{eqnarray}
\nonumber
\lim_{n \rightarrow \infty}\frac{1}{n}
{\rm Tr}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{{\bf y}_n}^{-1}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{{\bf y}_n,k}^{'}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{{\bf y}_n}^{-1}
\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{{\bf y}_n,\ell}^{'})
&=&
\label{eq: matrice variance limit 2}
\\
&&
\hspace{-4.5cm}
\int_{0}^{1}
{\rm Tr}({\bf S}_{x}^{-1}(f) {\bf S}_{x,k}^{'}(f) {\bf S}_{x}^{-1}(f){\bf S}_{x,\ell}^{'}(f))df.
\end{eqnarray}
<!-- end result-5 -->
<!-- result-6: body_md -->
\label{Result banded Toeplitz}
For  banded block-Toeplitz structured covariance $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{{\bf y}_n}$ satisfying ${\bf R}_x(k)={\bf 0}$ for $|k|>q$, 
the following upper bounds, which depend on ${\boldsymbol \theta}$, hold:
 
\begin{eqnarray}
\nonumber
|\frac{1}{n}{\boldsymbol \mu'}^T_{{\bf y}_n,k}\ \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{{\bf y}_n}^{-1}{\boldsymbol \mu}'_{{{\bf y}_n},\ell}
-
{\boldsymbol \mu'}^T_{{\bf x}_k}{\bf S}_{x}^{-1}(0){\boldsymbol \mu}'_{{\bf x}_\ell}|
&&
\\
\label{eq:Result banded Toeplitz1}
&&
\hspace{-5cm}
\le\frac{h(q)c_rM}{\sqrt{n}}    \| {\bf S}_x^{-1}(0)\|_2\|{\boldsymbol \mu}'_{{\bf x}_k}\|_2\|{\boldsymbol \mu}'_{{\bf x}_\ell}\|_2,
\end{eqnarray}
 
where $h(q) \stackrel{{\rm def}}{=}  \sqrt{q(q+1)(2q+1)/3}$.
 
\begin{eqnarray}
\nonumber
|\frac{1}{n}{\rm Tr}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{{\bf y}_n}^{-1}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{{\bf y}_n,k}^{'})
-
\int_{0}^{1}
{\rm Tr}({\bf S}_{x}^{-1}(f) {\bf S}_{x,k}^{'}(f))df|
\\
\label{eq:Result banded Toeplitz2}
&&
\hspace{-5.5cm}
\le \frac{2q^2m c_r(M\frac{c'_k}{c_1}+M'_k)}{n}+\frac{\delta_{n,S,S_k}}{n}
\end{eqnarray}
  
where $\frac{\delta_{n,S,S_k}}{n}$ bounds the Riemann sum approximation error:
$|\frac{1}{n}
{\rm Tr}\{{\rm Diag}
({\bf S}_{x,n}^{-1} {\bf S}_{x,n,k}^{'})\}
-\int_{0}^{1}
{\rm Tr}({\bf S}_{x}^{-1}(f) {\bf S}_{x,k}^{'}(f))df|$.
<!-- end result-6 -->
<!-- result-7: body_md -->
\label{limit of the three coefficients}
 
For an arbitrary distribution of the texture r.v. $\tau$ whether continuous, discrete, or mixed, subject to the
                                                                                                                                      
  constraint ${\rm E}(\tau)=1$, the sequences of coefficients $a_{i,mn}$, $i=0,1,2$ satisfy the following limits:
 
\begin{eqnarray}
\label{eq:lim a0}
\lim_{n\rightarrow \infty}a_{0,mn}
&=&
{\rm E}(\tau^{-1}), 
\\
\label{eq:lim a1}
\lim_{n\rightarrow \infty}a_{1,mn}
&=&
\frac{1}{2},
\\
\label{eq:lim a2}
\lim_{n\rightarrow \infty}n a_{2,mn}^{\rm Clas}
&=&
-\frac{(1-\beta)}{2m}\le 0,
\\
\label{eq:lim a2 SePa}
\lim_{n\rightarrow \infty}n a_{2,mn}^{\rm SePa}
&=&
\left\lbrace
\begin{array}{ll}
0& \mbox{if}\ \tau=1\  \mbox{(Gaussian case)}\\
-\frac{1}{2m}& \mbox{otherwise}\\
\end{array}
\right.
\end{eqnarray}
 
where
$\beta$ is the probability of the discrete component of the distribution of $\tau$ (i.e., $\beta  \stackrel{{\rm def}}{=}  \sum_{t;P(\tau=t)\ne 0}P(\tau=t)$.
<!-- end result-7 -->
<!-- head-1: body_md -->
\eqref{eq:lim a1} follows directly from
\eqref{eq:a0a1} and \eqref{eq:inequalities xi2}.
\eqref{eq:lim a2 SePa} follows from 
$na_{2,mn}^{\rm SePa}=
\frac{n}{\sigma^2_{\mathcal{Q}_{mn}}}- \frac{1}{2m}\xi_{2,mn}$
\eqref{eq:a2clsepa} with \eqref{eq:inequalities xi2} and 
$\frac{n}{\sigma^2_{\mathcal{Q}_{mn}}}=\frac{1}{n[{\rm E}(\tau^2)-1]+2{\rm E}(\tau^2)}$ derived from \eqref{eq:Stochastic representation CG b}
where ${\rm E}(\tau^2)=1$ i.f.f. $\tau=1$ from the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality.
In contrast, the proofs for \eqref{eq:lim a0} and \eqref{eq:lim a2} are significantly more involved and are provided in the Appendix.
\hfill
\mbox{\rule[0pt]{1.4ex}{1.4ex}}
<!-- end head-1 -->
<!-- result-8: body_md -->
\label{main result}
Under the assumptions stated in Section~\ref{sec:Preliminaries on multidimensional stationary SIRP}, the asymptotic FIM rate for a multidimensional stationary SIRP with arbitrary mean, has the following expression:
 
\begin{eqnarray}
\nonumber
\lim_{n \rightarrow \infty}
\frac{1}{n}\left({\rm FIM}_{y_n}(\boldsymbol{\theta})\right)_{k,\ell}
&=&
{\rm E}\left(\tau^{-1}\right) {\boldsymbol \mu}^{'T}_{x,k}
{\bf S}_{x}^{-1}(0)
{\boldsymbol \mu}_{x,\ell}'
\\
\nonumber
&&
\hspace{-2.5cm}
+\frac{1}{2}\int_{0}^{1}{\rm Tr}({\bf S}_{x}^{-1}(f) {\bf S}_{x,k}^{'}(f) {\bf S}_{x}^{-1}(f){\bf S}_{x,\ell}^{'}(f))df
\\
\nonumber
&&
\hspace{-2.5cm}
{+c}
\left(\int_{0}^{1}{\rm Tr}({\bf S}_{x}^{-1}(f) {\bf S}_{x,k}^{'}(f))df\right)
\\
\label{eq:Whittle's formula}
&&
\hspace{-1cm}
\left(\int_{0}^{1}{\rm Tr}({\bf S}_{x}^{-1}(f) {\bf S}_{x,\ell}^{'}(f))df\right),
\end{eqnarray}
 
where $c$ is given by the limit in \eqref{eq:lim a2} or \eqref{eq:lim a2 SePa}
depending on whether the density generator $g$ is known or unknown, respectively.
<!-- end result-8 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{decompositionSigma}
The following decomposition holds
 
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:banded block6}
{\bf W}_{n,m}^H \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{{\bf y}_n}{\bf W}_{n,m}
=
{\rm Diag}({\bf S}_{x,n})
+\boldsymbol{\Phi}_n,
\end{equation}
 
where $\boldsymbol{\Phi}_n$ is the $mn \times mn$ block structured matrix given by:
 
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:banded block7}
\boldsymbol{\Phi}_n
=
{\bf W}_{n,m}^H \boldsymbol{\Delta}_{n}{\bf W}_{n,m},
\end{equation}
 
where $ \boldsymbol{\Delta}_{n}$ is the  $nm \times nm$ block symmetric-Toeplitz matrix  whose first block row is $({\bf 0},..., {\bf 0},{\bf R}_x^T(q),...,{\bf R}_x^T(1))$.
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{block Schur}
 
The following inequality holds:
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:block Schur inequality}
\|{\boldsymbol \Delta}_{n}\|_2 \le \sqrt{r({ \boldsymbol \Delta}_{n}) c({ \boldsymbol \Delta}_{n}) }.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- head-2: body_md -->
Since ${\rm E}(\tau^{-2})<\infty$, $\tau^{-1}$ is square-integrable,
and the conditional expectation ${\rm E}(\tau^{-1}|\mathcal{Q}_{mn})$
is the orthogonal projection onto the subspace of
$\mathcal{Q}_{mn}$-measurable r.v.. Hence it
minimizes the mean-square error among all such variables; in
particular, for $\frac{mn}{\mathcal{Q}_{mn}}$ (square-integrable
for $mn>4$), 
${\rm E}(\tau^{-1}-z_n)^2
\le
{\rm E}\left(\tau^{-1}-\frac{mn}{\mathcal{Q}_{mn}}\right)^2$.
<!-- end head-2 -->
<!-- head-3: body_md -->
Because $\frac{\mathcal{Q}_{mn}}{mn}z_n$ is
$\mathcal{Q}_{mn}$-measurable, the identity
${\rm E}[X\,{\rm E}(Y|\mathcal{Q})]={\rm E}[XY]$ applied with
$X=\frac{\mathcal{Q}_{mn}}{mn}z_n$ and $Y=\tau^{-1}$ gives
<!-- end head-3 -->
<!-- head-4: body_md -->
Assume that $\tau$ is discretely distributed, and let
$t_1 < \dots < t_k < \dots < t_r$ denote its finitely many
positive values, with $P(\tau=t_k)=p_k$ and
$\Delta  \stackrel{{\rm def}}{=}  \min_{i \neq j}|t_i-t_j| > 0$.
Consider the $r$ disjoint intervals
$I_k  \stackrel{{\rm def}}{=}  [\,mn\,t_k(1-\epsilon),\, mn\,t_k(1+\epsilon)\,]$,
$k=1,\dots,r$ (with $\epsilon$ to be specified later). The key
quantity is the conditional probability
$P(\tau=t_k | \mathcal{Q}_{mn}=q)$ for $q \in I_k$, which is
controlled by the following lemma, proved in the  supplemental
material.
<!-- end head-4 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{conditional probability}
For $q \in I_k$, there exist $C_k>0$ and $c>0$, independent of
$n$, such that
 
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:conditional probability q k}
P(\tau=t_k | \mathcal{Q}_{mn}=q)
\ge
1-C_k\,e^{-cn}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- head-5: body_md -->
We now assume that $\tau$ is continuously distributed with a
continuous p.d.f. $p_\tau(t)$. Since
${\rm E}(\chi^2_{mn}/mn)=1$, the variance of the conditional
expectation can be written as
<!-- end head-5 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
\label{conditional}
Let $K  \stackrel{{\rm def}}{=}  [\alpha_-,\alpha_+]\subset (0,\infty)$.
There exists a constant $C_K>0$ such that, for every $q$
satisfying $\frac{q}{mn} \in K$,
 
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:conditiona expectation}
|{\rm E}(\frac{\chi_{mn}^2}{mn}|\mathcal{Q}_{mn}=q)-1|
\le \frac{C_K}{n}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
